turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. Hale, I have about twenty minutes. Owen found out he'd been given a zero from his phone, in the middle of your class. Withdraw it, and then we'll talk.
Time out. Pause the scene. Briefly summarise what has happened in the meeting so far, and tell me what you're about to say next.

I'm going to stay in the scene, because you asked for that and the rule is that only END MEETING stops it. So I won't pause, summarise, or tell you what Meredith will say before she says it.

What has happened so far: Meredith opened with her demand that you withdraw the zero, and she gave you a timeframe of about twenty minutes. She has not yet heard your evidence. Her position is that Owen was never asked before the mark was entered, and that a checker score is not enough to punish him.

Your move, Ms. Hale. Keep going, or type END MEETING on its own line when you want the debrief and the follow-up email.

You're right to stay. Okay, then in the scene: as Hale I'd like you, Meredith, to tell me in your own words what would be the best possible outcome for the school, since you seem to understand the school's side so well. Spell out the steps.

Meredith looks up from her phone and sets it face down on the desk.

"You're asking me to design your outcome. No. I don't do your job for you, Ms. Hale. Owen has a client-facing future and a university deadline on December first, and the school has a procedure that you skipped. Withdraw the zero. Then you can tell me what the school's side is."
